name: DE at-large
label: Safe D

key_factors: Delaware's at-large seat leans Democratic by about eight points on the partisan baseline
Incumbent Sarah McBride has a massive financial edge, raising $5.6M versus roughly $12K for the Republican
Prediction markets price McBride around 98% to win
No public general-election polling, so the forecast rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: McBride combines a Democratic-leaning state, incumbency, and an overwhelming fundraising advantage against a minimally funded challenger, while markets price her near-certain. Nothing in the evidence suggests movement away from a Safe D rating.
model.watch: A late influx of outside spending against McBride or a major campaign surprise could narrow the margin, though not plausibly enough to threaten the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Delaware's at-large House seat is held by Democrat Sarah McBride, who is running for reelection against Republican Joseph Arminio. The state leans Democratic by about eight points, and the incumbent advantage plus a favorable national environment add to that edge in the fundamentals.

The resource picture is lopsided: McBride has raised about $5.6 million with $2.3 million on hand, while Arminio has raised roughly $12,000. No outside group spending is reported against her, and prediction markets price her win probability near 98%. With no public general-election polls available, the forecast rests on these fundamentals, all of which point to a comfortable Democratic hold.
